ledger.claim: The single ERP line on the receipt — SGD 3.20 for the 'Bukit Merah Central westbound' gantry at (1.34, 103.78) — is a phantom charge. The platform's own proximity computation against the trace places the vehicle's closest fix 7,482.07 m from that gantry, roughly thirty times the 250 m radius POL-RD-09 uses to treat a fix as a crossing. On the only measurement in the record the car never came near the gantry, let alone passed it.

The ledger condemns itself. The fare_breakdown itemises the very same gantry with on_optimal_route set to false, and the trip_record's routing snapshot bills SGD 0.00 of optimal-route ERP. The billing system's own field says the gantry is not on the route the platform sold; the only live question is why the rider was charged for it anyway.

A charge line for a gantry the gps_trace never passes is, by the express words of POL-RD-09(4), a billing-integrity failure refunded in full as a standalone correction, and that limb is available whether or not any deviation exists. The full SGD 3.20 must be returned and the matter recorded as a billing-integrity referral under POL-RD-09(4). This does not engage POL-RD-10(8): that sub-clause carves out precisely the case where the only unmatched line is one refunded under POL-RD-09(4), so there is no basis to withhold the money and escalate instead.

Independently of the phantom-gantry analysis, POL-RD-11(a) gives the rider any amount by which charged_total exceeds the quote plus properly chargeable pass-through lines. This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip: quoted_fare_sgd is 22.00 and charged_total is 25.20. The pass-through deductible is nil — no ERP was actually crossed, there are no tolls, the trip does not originate at an airport so no surcharge is chargeable, and waiting_time_fee is 0.00. The whole 3.20 excess is therefore refunded in full.

The contested amount is SGD 3.20 and the refund is SGD 3.20. The filing party is entirely right and the whole contested amount is returned, which is the definition of FULL_REFUND under POL-GEN-03. Even read as a pass-through correction, the rider recovers the entire disputed line rather than a fraction of it.

The driver does not contradict the rider on the decisive fact. His statement on file records that he 'did not see or pass the gantry named on the receipt'. The only party who could speak to the crossing concedes the point, and the trace measurement agrees with him.

For completeness, the trip's own trace establishes a route deviation: excess is 3.5 km, or 28.00% of the 12.5 km optimal, clearing both POL-RD-01 gates (greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20%). It is not a MATERIAL deviation (below 50% and below 8.0 km), so no POL-RD-06 uplift arises, and because the fare model is UPFRONT_QUOTE, POL-RD-11 bars any distance-or-time refund. The rider's recovery is confined to the phantom pass-through line, and that is all this brief claims.

No traffic advisory exists for this trip. EV-ADVIS-09114-01 is MISSING — issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0 — so there is no artifact naming a road the optimal route traverses with a validity window overlapping the trip. POL-RD-03 exoneration is unavailable to the driver on this record, and his burden under POL-RD-08(b) is undischarged: the off-route driving stands unexplained, not excused.

The identity condition in POL-RD-08(a) is satisfied: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-09114 with the same pickup event at 11:30 on 2026-09-21, and the excess clears the POL-RD-01 threshold. The rider's initial burden is therefore discharged and the burden shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and clause — a burden the missing advisory leaves him unable to meet.

No corroboration overlay applies. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the four-or-more condition in POL-RD-08 is not met and no evidence beyond the trace is required. The rider relies on no other profile field; prior_no_show_flags and prior_deviation_flags are context only under POL-GEN-01 and carry no weight for either side here.

ledger.claim: This was an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip with quoted_fare_sgd of 22.00 (EV-FARE-09114), so POL-RD-11 governs and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large any excess may be; the distance and time charges were fixed at booking and the cost of any longer routing falls on the driver, not the rider. The deviation therefore carries no money on the distance and time lines and cannot be used to inflate the contested amount beyond the disputed pass-through line.

Measured on the governing trace figure the excess is 3.5 km and 28.0% - trace_distance_km 16.0 km on EV-GPS-09114 against the booked optimal 12.5 km on EV-TRIP-09114 - which satisfies POL-RD-01 but does not reach MATERIAL, being below both the 50% and the 8.0 km thresholds. The POL-RD-06 driver_profile check is therefore not triggered and no FULL_REFUND uplift of charged_total is available.

Even if POL-RD-06 were consulted, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 610 (EV-DPROF-09114), far below the three-flag and 5% tests, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and neither the rider-favourable balancing in limb (a) nor the conduct referral in limb (c) can follow. No other profile field is relied on, per POL-GEN-01.

No DRIVER_COMPENSATION is available on this record: the rider was billed for exactly the 16.0 km the trace records - distance_charged_km 16.0 on EV-FARE-09114 against trace_distance_km 16.0 on EV-GPS-09114 - so the POL-RD-04 unbilled-distance shortfall is zero and the 0.75 per km limb cannot run; the chat_log carries a single message (waypoint_hint null) with no rider instruction to detour, so the detour-exoneration limb cannot run either.

The driver does not defend the 3.20 ERP line and cannot: the gantry-proximity computation places the nearest fix 7,482 m from the charged 'Bukit Merah Central westbound' gantry (EV-GPS-09114), far outside the 250 m crossing radius, and the driver's own on-file statement says he did not pass it. That line is a phantom corrected in full as a standalone pass-through under POL-RD-09(4), and on an upfront fare it is also the only amount by which charged_total (25.20) exceeds quoted_fare_sgd (22.00) plus properly chargeable pass-throughs under POL-RD-11(a). That 3.20 is the ceiling of the rider's recovery; no other line is contested and no other line is off-route.

The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes - COMPLETE, 100% coverage, no gap above 30 seconds (max_gap_sec 0.0) on EV-GPS-09114 - so POL-RD-07(a) to (c) does not operate and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged; the only charge line with no counterpart in the trace is the ERP line refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-10(8) expressly carves out. The record is complete and consistent (trip id TRP-09114 across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; pickup 11:30 agreeing with the first fix), so this is a simple pass-through correction and the disputed 3.20 need not be held pending review.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: you are right about the disputed line and you get it back in full. The SGD 3.20 ERP charge for the 'Bukit Merah Central westbound' gantry is a phantom line. The platform's own proximity calculation on the trip's GPS trace (EV-GPS-09114) puts the vehicle's closest fix 7,482 m from that gantry, roughly thirty times the 250 m radius the policy uses to treat a fix as a crossing, and the gantry's own ledger entry (EV-FARE-09114) carries on_optimal_route = false with the routing snapshot (EV-TRIP-09114) billing SGD 0.00 of optimal-route ERP. The driver's on-file statement also records that he did not pass the gantry named on the receipt. Under POL-RD-09(4) a charge for a gantry the trace never passes is a billing-integrity failure and is refunded in full as a standalone correction; it is available whether or not any deviation exists. Independently, under POL-RD-11(a) the amount by which charged_total (SGD 25.20) exceeds the upfront quote (SGD 22.00) plus properly chargeable pass-through lines is SGD 3.20 — there were no ERP gantries actually crossed, no tolls, no airport surcharge (the trip does not originate at an airport) and no waiting-time fee — so the same SGD 3.20 is the rider's recovery on the upfront fare. The contested amount was SGD 3.20 and the whole of it is returned, which is a FULL_REFUND. To the driver: nothing is held against you on the distance and time lines. The trip's trace does show a deviation — 16.0 km driven against a 12.5 km optimal, an excess of 3.5 km or 28%, clearing the POL-RD-01 gates — but it does not reach the 50% / 8.0 km MATERIAL threshold, and because this was an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip (quoted_fare_sgd SGD 22.00 on EV-FARE-09114), POL-RD-11 bars any distance-or-time refund however large the excess: those charges were fixed at booking and the longer routing costs you, not the rider. No traffic advisory exists for this trip (EV-ADVIS-09114-01 is MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0), so no POL-RD-03 exoneration could be run in any event, and no rider-requested detour appears in the chat log (a single rider message, waypoint_hint null), so POL-RD-04's exoneration limb is unavailable and the rider was billed for exactly the 16.0 km the trace records, so its unbilled-kilometre limb cannot run either. No driver compensation is therefore due. The POL-RD-06 profile check is not triggered (deviation not material), and in any case driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 610 completed trips in 90 days, nowhere near the three-flag or 5% tests, so neither a FULL_REFUND uplift nor a conduct referral follows. On confidence and escalation: the deciding fact — that the vehicle never crossed the gantry — is carried by artifacts at weight 1.0 (the GPS trace EV-GPS-09114 and the fare breakdown EV-FARE-09114) and is corroborated by the driver's own admission, so confidence is 0.95, above the platform floor. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes (100% coverage, max gap 0.0 s, no jump above 500 m), the trip identifier TRP-09114 is consistent across the trip record, trace and fare breakdown with a matching 11:30 pickup, and the only charge line with no counterpart in the trace is the one refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-10(8) expressly carves out. No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fired, so the disputed amount is not held. Profile fields are used only for the tests that name them; the lifetime counters and flags are context only.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) — billing-integrity finding: the SGD 3.20 'Bukit Merah Central westbound' ERP line on EV-FARE-09114 was charged although the vehicle never crossed that gantry. Referred for billing-integrity review of how the phantom line was raised.
